summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of T2 paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, and prior episodes of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) was admitted with acute confusion, severe headache, and transient bilateral vision loss. She had been experiencing worsening chronic pain and was found to have markedly elevated blood pressure. Brain imaging, including CT and MRI, confirmed PRES with characteristic white matter changes. Urinalysis showed signs of infection, and culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae, indicating a complicated urinary tract infection. Antibiotics were initially withheld due to atypical presentation but were started with ertapenem after lack of mental status improvement. Blood pressure was controlled with captopril and then transitioned to lisinopril. A PICC line was placed to complete a 7-day course of IV antibiotics at home. Her mental status normalized, and she was discharged home with home health services for IV antibiotic administration and neurology follow-up to evaluate for sympathetic dysregulation.
